artifact_review: The Router identified a 'texture_anomaly' (severity 1.5) and 'structural_collapse' (severity 2.0). I agree with the texture anomaly assessment; the wing scales lack micro-definition, appearing painterly. However, I believe the severity of the leg-stem junction issue is underestimated. The topology mask shows a clean boundary for the main body, but the legs themselves are barely resolved and seem to merge into the stem without clear contact points. This 'melting' is a classic AI artifact in insect generation. The perceptual quality auditor noted 'slight compression,' which aligns with the texture smudging. The geometric depth auditor did not flag grounding failure, but the visual ambiguity of the legs remains a structural defect. I will adjust the artifact score down to reflect this structural weakness more heavily than the Router did.
alignment_reasoning: The fine_grained_classifier confirmed the class 'ringlet' with high confidence (logit 7.18), significantly higher than the next candidate. All visible morphological features (clubbed antennae, eyespot arrangement, brown coloration, closed wings) match the taxonomy perfectly. The only missing verification is the forelegs, which are obscured. Thus, alignment is near-perfect for visible features.
artifact_reasoning: While the overall structure is sound, there are notable artifacts. 1) Texture smudging on the wings (painterly effect instead of scales). 2) Structural ambiguity at the leg-stem interface; the legs do not clearly grip the stem but rather blend into it, indicating a minor structural collapse/melting artifact. 3) Slight compression/noise noted by the perceptual auditor. These issues prevent a perfect artifact score, placing it below the 'high' reference (4.0) but well above the 'mid' reference (3.0).
key_defects: Painterly wing texture lacking scale detail
